The “Quality Staircase” shows how MTF requirements should be reduced throughout the manufacturing process to balance image quality with yield. 2. For machine vision, you may consider image quality factors where if your system does not provide sufficient quality, the computer vision task will fail. Once you have decided on the components that will comprise your imaging system, you should build and test a collection of sample cameras. If you use a single golden sample to set your pass-fail criteria, you would want to repeat several tests with that sample in order to determine its minimum quality in the presence of sources of variation because of sensor noise and other factors. But if you only consider a single “golden sample”, you may find that other cameras that are not quite as good as the golden sample but “good enough” will fail.

results.title: Factory Acceptance Test : Ensuring Quality Before Shipment
results.content: Read more about these purposes Product Sourcing, Product Testing, Quality Control # Factory Acceptance Test (FAT): Key Principles, Processes, and Best Practices * Understanding the Basics of Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) + What Is Factory Acceptance Test (FAT)? + Core Principles of Effective Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) - Comprehensive Coverage with Strategic Focus * Step-by-Step Implementation of Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) - Set up the test environment: - Real-time testing and documentation: - Focus on high-risk items: Final Acceptance and Documentation Delivery * Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) Applications Across Industries Industrial Equipment: CNC Machine Tools Electronic Products: Servers or Power Station Large Machinery: Automated Production Lines * Client Examples of Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) Implementation * Common FAT Challenges and Solutions * How Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) Differs from Other Quality Checks * Emerging Trends in Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) + Digital Transformation: Virtual FAT and Digital Twins + Intelligent Testing with AI and Automation + Global Collaboration: Remote FAT and Standard Unification In the industrial production lifecycle, a link directly determines whether products leave the factory qualified and meet customer requirements: the **Factory Acceptance Test (FAT)**. *Example: If a customer specifies an industrial oven must reach 300°C, FAT explicitly tests for this temperature, not just basic heating functionality.* Beyond customer-specific requirements, FAT must align with industry regulations and international standards. Adequate preparation lays the groundwork for successful FAT: Manufacturers and customers collaborate to outline test criteria, pass/fail benchmarks, and excluded items (e.g., on-site installation steps). * #### **Focus on high-risk items**: Critical tests (e.g., sterility checks for medical devices) may require video recording and customer witnessing to ensure traceability. Commissioning optimizes on-site performance post-installation (e.g., tuning PID parameters), while FAT verifies shipment readiness: * **Purpose**: FAT = “qualified for delivery”; Commissioning = “optimal operation.” * **Content**: FAT = pass/fail tests; Commissioning = dynamic parameter adjustments. ## **Conclusion** **Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) is the last line of defense against substandard products reaching customers.** By following its principles, adhering to structured processes, and adapting to new technologies, manufacturers and customers can ensure product reliability, reduce risks, and strengthen supply chain trust.

results.title: Why aren’t “PASS/FAIL” criteria sufficient for controlling manufacturing yield and quality? - Quality Line
results.content: Home > Smart manufacturing > Why aren’t “PASS/FAIL” criteria sufficient for controlling manufacturing yield and quality? # Why aren’t “PASS/FAIL” criteria sufficient for controlling manufacturing yield and quality? AI technology, Digital and smart factory, Digital Factory, Manufacturing analytics, Smart manufacturing. Managing a mass manufacturing process is always a challenge because hundreds of tasks must be successfully completed before your products are ready to be shipped to your customers. At every stage of the production flow—from incoming raw materials to the final stage before delivery—we implement testing processes. But how do we actually use this data to optimize quality and yield, minimizing defective products and customer returns? To avoid unexpected downtime, waste, and defective products, we need to collect and interpret all relevant data and turn it into actionable insights. * Continuous collection and interpretation of test and process data for each unit, process, and plant. * Automated detection of quality and yield issues. Why aren’t “PASS/FAIL” criteria sufficient for controlling first pass yield and manufacturing quality? Many manufacturers rely on a simple “PASS” or “FAIL” test criterion for each parameter. However, when evaluating product quality, this approach is insufficient. 1. **Technical challenges** in integrating and collecting test data from automated equipment across the manufacturing line. 2. **Information overload.** In mass production, it’s nearly impossible to process all the detailed data collected from testing stations. Detailed analysis typically happens only when a critical quality issue arises, requiring root cause investigation. Due to the difficulty of managing vast amounts of testing data, manufacturers often default to minimal “PASS/FAIL” criteria, discarding valuable detailed information. This oversimplification limits the ability to control processes and improve quality and yield. Leveraging new technologies for fast and scalable data integration allows manufacturers to collect and analyze data in real time. * Assurance of the highest product quality for customers. By focusing on accurate and actionable data, manufacturers can effectively control the quality of their processes and improve overall yield. ### **One of our experts will host a free live demo for you and show which valuable insights you can get from our Advanced Manufacturing Analytics**. ### **Check how our AI technology automatically integrates with any of your manufacturing data to power the analytics**.
